mainEntity.name: How is lean body mass different from muscle mass?

acceptedAnswer.text: Lean body mass includes muscle, but also bone, organs, and water — it's a broader measure than muscle mass alone, which is why LBM is typically higher than an estimate of muscle tissue by itself.

mainEntity.name: Why does the formula use height as well as weight?

acceptedAnswer.text: Height helps account for overall body frame size, improving the accuracy of the estimate compared to using weight alone.

mainEntity.name: Which lean body mass formula is most accurate?

acceptedAnswer.text: No single formula is best for everyone. Boer is widely used and generally reasonable for typical builds; if you have a measured body fat percentage (for example from DEXA), calculating lean mass directly from it is more accurate than any height-and-weight formula.
Fat-free mass index is lean mass divided by height in metres squared — like BMI, but counting only lean tissue. It helps compare muscularity between people of different heights.
